title: Filtered colimits of standard normalized coefficient dg algebras
statement:
Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $D$ and $S$ be commutative rings with a homomorphism $D\to S$. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed partially ordered set and $(E_i)_{i\in I}$ a system of commutative $D$-algebras with compatible $D$-algebra maps $E_i\to E_j$ for $i\leq j$. Let $E=\varinjlim_i E_i$ be its ordinary algebra colimit, meaning the disjoint-union presentation modulo eventual equality, with operations induced at common upper bounds. No transition map is assumed injective or flat. For any commutative $D$-algebra $B$, use the unmodified standard simplicial polynomial resolution $P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(B/D)$ and its functorial maps of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. Thus $P^{\mathrm{std}}_n(B/D)=(F_DU)^{n+1}B$, where $F_D(T)=D[T]$ and $U$ is the underlying-set functor. Put $R^{\mathrm{std}}_B=N(P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(B/D))$, using the quotient normalization and shuffle multiplication of [lem-sfb-simplicial-algebra-shuffle-normalization], including this unmodified resolution when $B=D$. Set $C^{\mathrm{std}}_B=S\otimes_D R^{\mathrm{std}}_B$, with tensor taken degreewise [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], $S$ in degree zero, and the induced differential and dg multiplication.

The functorial comparison
$$\varinjlim_{i\in I} C^{\mathrm{std}}_{E_i}\longrightarrow C^{\mathrm{std}}_E$$
is an isomorphism of dg $S$-algebras, where the colimit is degreewise on the underlying $D$-modules, with multiplication induced at common stages. More explicitly, every finite collection of homogeneous elements of $C^{\mathrm{std}}_E$ admits homogeneous lifts of the same degrees at one stage. If such elements are already specified at a stage and finitely many equalities between homogeneous expressions obtained by addition, multiplication, differential, signs, and specified scalars from $S$ hold after passage to $C^{\mathrm{std}}_E$, those equalities hold after passage to some common later stage. Zero rings and zero modules are allowed.

source.place: Tag 08PM (definition-standard-resolution) and Tag 08S9 (lemma-colimit-cotangent-complex), proof: both free polynomial algebra and underlying-set functors commute with filtered colimits; quotient normalization from simplicial.tex Tag 019A (lemma-decompose-associated-complexes). The dg-algebra and finite differential-equation formulation is an agent refinement, not the cotangent-complex statement of 08S9.

proof.text: First unpack the polynomial universal property. For any small diagram of sets $T_i$ with colimit $T$, and any commutative $D$-algebra $A$, compatible algebra maps $D[T_i]\to A$ are exactly compatible functions $T_i\to U(A)$: restrict to the variables, or evaluate at their images. Such functions give exactly one function $T\to U(A)$, hence exactly one algebra map $D[T]\to A$. Thus the canonical cocone $D[T_i]\to D[T]$ is an algebra colimit. This is a direct application of the cited universal property, with no assumption that any $T_i\to T_j$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 08S9 (lemma-colimit-cotangent-complex), proof: the free polynomial functor commutes with colimits; universal-property argument expanded

proof.text: Put $G=F_DU$. Induct on $k\geq0$ to show that the underlying sets of $G^kE_i\to G^kE$ form a directed colimit. For $k=0$ this is precisely the disjoint-union modulo eventual equality presentation of $E$ in the hypothesis. Given the assertion for $k$, Step 1 says that $D[U(G^kE)]$ is the algebra colimit of $D[U(G^kE_i)]$. The cited algebra-to-module colimit theorem and the module elementwise theorem say that this cocone has stage representatives and eventual equality on underlying sets. These two properties identify its underlying set with the disjoint-union colimit: send a representative to its image; surjectivity is the first property and injectivity is the second after moving two stages to a common upper bound. This proves the induction step. For $k=n+1$ we obtain the canonical algebra and underlying $D$-module colimit cocone $P^{\mathrm{std}}_n(E_i/D)\to P^{\mathrm{std}}_n(E/D)$. The standard-resolution node identifies these iterates and supplies their functorial maps, which commute with every face and degeneracy.

source.place: Tags 08PM (definition-standard-resolution) and 08S9 (lemma-colimit-cotangent-complex), proof: iterate the two colimit-preserving functors

proof.text: Write $P_{i,n}=P^{\mathrm{std}}_n(E_i/D)$, $P_n=P^{\mathrm{std}}_n(E/D)$, and $J_{i,n}=\sum_{r<n}\operatorname{im}s_r$, $J_n=\sum_{r<n}\operatorname{im}s_r$. A class in $P_n/J_n$ lifts by choosing a representative in $P_n$ and then a stage representative using Step 2. If $x,y\in P_{i,n}$ have the same class in $P_n/J_n$, then their image difference is $\sum_{r<n}s_r(z_r)$ for some $z_r\in P_{n-1}$: each degeneracy is $D$-linear, so coefficients and repeated terms can be absorbed in $z_r$. Lift the finitely many $z_r$ to one stage $j\geq i$. The difference $x_j-y_j-\sum_{r<n}s_r(z_{r,j})$ has zero image in $P_n$, hence vanishes at a later stage $l$ by the module elementwise theorem. Therefore $[x_l]=[y_l]$ in $P_{l,n}/J_{l,n}$. At $n=0$ the sum is empty and this is just eventual equality in $P_0$.

source.place: Tag 019A (lemma-decompose-associated-complexes), degeneracy summand and quotient normalization; the directed-colimit argument uses Algebra Tags 00D6 and 00D7

proof.text: Step 3 verifies both hypotheses of the module-colimit criterion for the cocone $P_{i,n}/J_{i,n}\to P_n/J_n$. Consequently $N(P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(E/D))$ is the degreewise $D$-module colimit of the stage normalizations. The differential is the quotient of $\sum_r(-1)^rd_r$; each comparison commutes with each $d_r$ by Step 2, so it commutes with this differential. Positive degrees are zero at every stage and at the limit. All indices remain in the given small nonempty directed poset; no change of index category or universe is involved.

source.place: Tag 019A (lemma-decompose-associated-complexes), quotient complex; Algebra Tags 00D6 and 00D7 give the elementwise colimit criterion

proof.text: Apply the tensor-colimit theorem in each degree to the constant ring system $A_i=D$, the constant module system $M_i=S$ with identity transitions, and $N_i=N(P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(E_i/D))^m$. The colimits of the constant systems are $D$ and $S$ because the index poset is nonempty and directed. Step 4 identifies the third colimit. Thus the canonical map $\varinjlim_i(S\otimes_DN_i)\to S\otimes_D\varinjlim_iN_i$ is a $D$-linear isomorphism, induced by $s\otimes x\mapsto s\otimes\iota_i(x)$. It is $S$-linear since multiplying a pure tensor by $t\in S$ replaces $s$ by $ts$ on both sides; pure tensors generate. Naturality with respect to the degree differentials proves that these maps form a chain isomorphism. This uses ordinary tensor products and their colimit property, so it requires no flatness of $S$ or of any transition map.

source.place: Tag 00DD (lemma-tensor-products-commute-with-limits), fixed-ring specialization; the cited varying-ring node includes naturality

proof.text: For homogeneous pure tensors of degrees $-p,-q$, the multiplication is $(s\otimes[x])(t\otimes[y])=st\otimes([x]\mathbin{\mathrm{sh}}[y])$. In each summand of the displayed shuffle formula, the stage-to-limit algebra map preserves the degeneracy strings, the product, the sign, and the resulting quotient class; therefore it preserves their finite sum. Hence the maps of Step 5 preserve multiplication on pure tensors, and bilinearity extends this equality to all homogeneous elements. They preserve the unit $1\otimes[1]$ as well. The stage maps are dg $S$-algebra maps by functorial normalization. Products on their degreewise module colimit are defined by moving two representatives to a common stage; independence follows by moving any two choices and their eventual equalities to a further common stage. Each dg law then follows by representing its finitely many inputs at one stage. Thus the chain isomorphism of Step 5 is exactly the asserted dg $S$-algebra comparison and is an isomorphism as such: applying its bijective components to a product or differential shows that its inverse also preserves them.

source.place: Tag 019A (lemma-decompose-associated-complexes), additive quotient model; multiplication is the explicit shuffle formula of the cited normalization node, checked term by term (agent refinement)

proof.text: The module elementwise theorem applied degreewise to Step 5 lifts each prescribed homogeneous element in its own degree. Choose a common upper bound of the finitely many resulting stages; an empty collection can be placed at any stage, since $I$ is nonempty. For the equation assertion, evaluate every specified homogeneous expression at its given stage. Its image is the same expression at the limit: this follows recursively from preservation of addition, multiplication, differential, signs and the $S$-action in Steps 5 and 6. For each of the finitely many equalities, subtract its two sides in their common degree. The resulting element has zero image at the limit, so the module elementwise theorem makes it zero at some later stage. A common upper bound of those finitely many stages makes all the equalities true simultaneously. Positive-degree inputs are zero and lift as zero. Zero rings and zero modules cause no exception; in particular the argument always uses $P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(D/D)=G^{\bullet+1}D$, without replacing it by the constant resolution.

lean.statement: theorem filtered_colimit (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra D S] {I : Type u} [PartialOrder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (F : I ⥤ CommAlgCat.{u} D) (c : Cocone F) (_hc : IsColimit c) : Nonempty (IsColimit ((coefficients D K S).mapCocone c)) ∧ (∀ m : ℤ, Nonempty (IsColimit ((degree D K S m).mapCocone c))) ∧ (∀ (l : Cocone (F ⋙ coefficients D K S)) (hl : IsColimit l), ∃ e : l.pt ≅ (coefficients D K S).obj c.pt, e.hom = hl.desc ((coefficients D K S).mapCocone c)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (d : Fin n → ℤ) (x : ∀ a : Fin n, (degree D K S (d a)).obj c.pt), ∃ (i : I) (y : ∀ a : Fin n, (degree D K S (d a)).obj (F.obj i)), ∀ a : Fin n, (degree D K S (d a)).map (c.ι.app i) (y a) = x a) ∧ (∀ (i : I) (n : ℕ) (d : Fin n → ℤ) (x y : ∀ a : Fin n, (degree D K S (d a)).obj (F.obj i)), (∀ a : Fin n, (degree D K S (d a)).map (c.ι.app i) (x a) = (degree D K S (d a)).map (c.ι.app i) (y a)) → ∃ (j : I) (h : i ≤ j), ∀ a : Fin n, (degree D K S (d a)).map (F.map (homOfLE h)) (x a) = (degree D K S (d a)).map (F.map (homOfLE h)) (y a))
